title: Compactness of abundance in asymmetric hypergraph removal lemmas
summary: Fix an integer $r\ge 2$ and a finite simple $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with at least one edge and no isolated vertices. An $n$-vertex $r$-graph is $ε$-far from being $F$-free if at least $εn^r$ edges must be deleted to destroy every copy of $F$. A finite $r$-graph $H$ is $F$-abundant if there are constants $c,C>0$ such that every sufficiently large $ε$-far host contains at least $cε^C n^{v(H)}$ labelled copies of $H$. A family is $F$-abundant when one member has this lower bound in each host, although the member may depend on the host and on $ε$, while $c$ and $C$ are common to the family.…
